title: Four emissions trading scheme changes with implications for E&P firms | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Wood Mackenzie reads the European Commission's proposed EU ETS review (targeting 2028 implementation, aligned to a 90% net cut by 2040) as lowering extreme price-spike risk while making the long-term carbon price path more predictable but lower, with E&P firms told to treat ETS shifts as commercially material.

insights.claim: Carbon policy has become a key factor in commercial decision making for oil and gas E&P firms, many of which must comply with Emissions Trading Schemes in several jurisdictions.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Include ETS changes in E&P valuation and capital allocation models.
insights.quote: carbon policy has become a key factor in commercial decision making for oil and gas exploration and production (E&P)

insights.claim: The European Commission's proposed EU ETS review, aimed at 2028 implementation, aligns carbon market rules with the EU target of 90% net emissions reduction by 2040 versus 1990.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Sets the regulatory frame for EU carbon price expectations through 2040.
insights.locator: The European Commission ETS review aims to trade pressures for incentives

insights.claim: The proposal lowers the Linear Reduction Factor, cuts the Market Stability Reserve intake rate, removes its invalidation mechanism and lowers its buffer, and changes free allocation phase-out timelines by sector carbon-leakage risk.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Supply-side loosening of the cap mechanics is the lever behind lower expected prices.

insights.claim: At least 50% of ETS auction revenues would be directed to decarbonisation, with an Industrial Decarbonisation Bank Fund financing projects first-come first-served before moving to competitive bidding that prioritises lowest abatement cost.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Early funding favours shovel-ready decarbonisation projects.

insights.claim: The proposal widens coverage in aviation, maritime and waste, and allows centralised purchase of domestic carbon dioxide removals, offsets from non-EU countries, and accounting of embedded emissions in non-permanent CCU products at release rather than capture.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Opens demand channels for removals and offsets; watch CCU accounting.

insights.claim: If adopted, the proposals reduce the risk of extreme end-game EU carbon price spikes without removing most reduction obligations, making the long-term price trajectory more predictable but lower.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Lower expected EU carbon prices ease compliance cost for emitters; price tail risk falls.
insights.quote: The long-term price trajectory will be more predictable albeit lower

insights.claim: Support under the plan depends on the credibility of each company's decarbonisation plans, and the Industrial Decarbonisation Bank could pull hard-to-abate sectors toward building capacity significantly earlier.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Credible decarbonisation plans become a funding differentiator.

insights.claim: The proposal implies a more collaborative EU role in global carbon markets, with non-EU companies benefiting via international credit mechanisms from 2036 and non-EU countries able to opt in to price aviation and maritime emissions and share revenue, while raising questions for CBAM.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Watch how the CBAM design interacts with international credits.

insights.claim: Three further ETS developments flagged as material for E&P are the EU integration path for carbon removals and offsets, Australia's Safeguard Mechanism review for 2031-2035, and revamped California and Québec cap-and-invest programmes.
insights.speaker: Stefania Albarosa
insights.so_what: Monitor these three jurisdictions for E&P compliance cost shifts.
